newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's NSW aims to usurp Singapore by 2005.
newsitem.headline: Australia's NSW aims to usurp Singapore by 2005.

text.p: The government of Australia's most populous state, New South Wales (NSW), intends to use the 2000 Olympics as an opportunity to boost Sydney as an Asia/Pacific location for business and investment at Singapore's expense.

Treasurer Michael Egan, delivering the state's 1997/98 (June 30) budget in state parliament, said the international focus in the lead-up to the Olympics provided Sydney, NSW and Australia an opportunity to sell themselves that may never be repeated.
"It's an opportunity we won't miss," he said. "New south Wales will also be stepping up its campaign to attract Asia/Pacific regional headquarters," Egan said.
"We have set 2005 as the target date for overtaking Singapore as a preferred Asia/Pacific headquarters location," Egan said in his budget speech.
The Olympic Business Round Table Committee had already formulated the strategies for promoting Sydney, NSW and Australia as a "first class" location for business and investment, he said.

Egan noted that Investment 2000, an investment promotion campaign jointly sponsored and funded by the state government, federal government owned telecommunications company Telstra, and Westpac Banking Corp, was already underway.
